description.value: McKitrick Garden is a publicly accessible garden operated by the City of Delta as part of its environmental sustainability initiatives. Situated in the Delta municipality of Metro Vancouver, it appears to serve an educational or demonstration role connected to the city's environmental programmes. Visiting cyclists would find a free, open-access green space, though specific visitor facilities are not documented on the city's website.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website fetch succeeded but returned only City of Delta navigation boilerplate — no substantive content about McKitrick Garden itself was captured in the prefetch. All amenity fields must therefore default to null as there is no positive or negative evidence. OSM tags confirm it is a public garden (garden:type=public, access=yes) operated by the City of Delta under its Environmental Initiatives programme, but no cyclist-specific facilities are attested anywhere. A location discrepancy exists: the OSM record assigns community 'Richmond' while the operator is 'City of Delta' and coordinates (~49.147°N, 122.917°W) place the garden in Delta, not Richmond.
concerns: Website prefetch returned only site-wide navigation boilerplate; no content specific to McKitrick Garden was captured, leaving all amenity fields unverifiable.

Community field in OSM record is 'Richmond', but the operator is 'City of Delta' and coordinates (~49.147°N, 122.917°W) place the site in Delta — not Richmond. Possible data entry error in the community assignment.
No street address is recorded in OSM, making it difficult for cyclists to locate the garden.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: The garden is publicly accessible and free to enter, which could suit a touring cyclist, but no cyclist amenities (bike parking, water, washrooms) could be confirmed due to the website returning only navigation content. Manual verification of on-site facilities is needed before a confident include or exclude decision can be made.
enrichment_extras.notes: This garden is listed under the City of Delta's Environmental Initiatives section, suggesting it may be a demonstration or educational garden rather than a conventional public park. A site visit or direct enquiry with the City of Delta Parks department would clarify available facilities.
